SECTION: ADMISSION CUTOFF ADVICE: IS THE GWA CUTOFF STRICT? (ADDITION TO THE ANNEX A CUTOFFS)
ADMISSION CUTOFF ADVICE: IS THE GWA CUTOFF STRICT? (ADDITION TO THE ANNEX A CUTOFFS)
Source: strictness and lower-cutoff advice from campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026); cutoff values are from the LSPU Admission Guidelines, 1st Sem AY 2026-2027, Annex A above; exam and interview from the LSPU website admission pages. Cutoffs may change each year.
The GWA cutoff is strict. If your GWA is below the minimum for the program you want, you cannot be admitted to it; your only option is to choose another program with a lower cutoff.
Example: a GWA of 86 qualifies only for the GWA-85 programs.
Cutoffs for 1st Sem AY 2026-2027: GWA 85 for the three BS Information Technology majors, BS Criminology and BS Hospitality Management (5 programs); GWA 87 for BS Fisheries, BTLE and BTVTE (3); GWA 88 for BS Psychology, both BS Business Administration majors and BS Tourism Management (4); GWA 90 for Accountancy, Computer Science, Food Technology, Nutrition and Dietetics, Physical Education, all five BS Education majors and Elementary Education (11).
Meeting the cutoff is not enough by itself: applicants must still pass the entrance exam and interview.

PROGRAM: Bachelor of Science in Information Technology - Major in Web and Mobile Application Development
College: College of Computer Studies (CCS)
Degree: Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (BSIT)
Major: Web and Mobile Application Development
Duration: 4 years

Overview: Combines core IT fundamentals with specialized training in building websites and mobile applications, including UI/UX design.

Skills developed:
- Web Application Development
- Mobile Application Development
- UI/UX Design

Career and job outcomes:
- Web/Mobile Application Developer: Builds websites and mobile applications for businesses or as an independent/freelance developer.

Admission requirement:
- Minimum General Weighted Average (GWA): 85.0
- Note: Annex A gives one GWA (85) for BSIT overall; per-major cutoffs are not broken out. CCS gives priority to STEM and ICT/ICTS strand applicants.

Board/licensure status:
- Not a board program (no PRC licensure examination is required for this degree).

Regulatory basis (CHED): CMO No. 25, s.

- Minimum General Weighted Average (GWA): 90.0

- Function effectively as part of a development team, communicating technical work clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

h:definition: A foreign applicant who graduated from a high school abroad and has not enrolled in the University may be admitted to the freshman class if they (1) submit complete secondary-school academic documents; (2) qualify in an accepted national or international examination: GCE with 3 ordinary-level and 2 advanced-level passes, or SAT with a minimum total score of 1200, or an International Baccalaureate Diploma, or an equivalent examination; and (3) if their native language or medium of instruction in secondary school is not English, score at least 500 (paper-based) or 173 (computer-based) on the TOEFL. Filipinos who graduated from a secondary school abroad and apply for freshman admission must meet the same requirements. An applicant transferring from another Philippine school should secure a permit to transfer from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED).

h:audience: Foreign applicants, Filipinos who studied abroad
h:definition: A foreign applicant who graduated from a high school abroad and has not enrolled in the University may be admitted to the freshman class if they (1) submit complete secondary-school academic documents; (2) qualify in an accepted national or international examination: GCE with 3 ordinary-level and 2 advanced-level passes, or SAT with a minimum total score of 1200, or an International Baccalaureate Diploma, or an equivalent examination; and (3) if their native language or medium of instruction in secondary school is not English, score at least 500 (paper-based) or 173 (computer-based) on the TOEFL. Filipinos who graduated from a secondary school abroad and apply for freshman admission must meet the same requirements. An applicant transferring from another Philippine school should secure a permit to transfer from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED).
